title: Keyboard Manager settings lines enable/disable randomly during edit
summary: This Keyboard Manager report is already covered by merged upstream work: PR #49287 contains a follow-up commit that fixes mappings silently turning off when ListView row recycling re-fires the enabled-toggle handler during list refresh.
next_action: Draft a maintainer comment pointing the reporter to merged PR #49287 and ask for a retest on a build newer than 0.101.2362 before opening any new design track.

confidence.rationale: The merged fix commit names the same symptom, explains the exact ListView recycling mechanism, and touches the precise toggle handler used by the affected editor rows.

linked_work.title: [Keyboard Manager] Search, filter and bulk-delete for the remapping list

judgment.rationale: Merged PR #49287 already contains a Keyboard Manager editor fix for mappings randomly switching OFF during list refresh, which matches both the original report and the later reproduction on 0.101.2362 stable.
evidence: The original report says that after adding or removing a mapping row, other Keyboard Manager entries become randomly enabled or disabled.

A later commenter reproduces the same issue on PowerToys v0.101.2362 stable with a mix of Keys, Text, and Disabled remappings and adds that some mappings appear enabled but do not take effect until toggled again; a recording link is attached.

`src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml` binds each `MappingEnabledToggle` to `IsActive` for remappings, text mappings, program shortcuts, URL shortcuts, and disabled rows.

`src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs` now contains an explicit guard in `ToggleSwitch_Toggled` plus an explanatory comment stating that ListView container recycling during filtering, bulk-delete reloads, or scrolling previously re-fired `Toggled` and flipped the wrong mapping's persisted active state.

Merged PR #49287 includes commit `ba331c72d5eb6d164313dd9b2a4c5bf6373bf81f` titled `[Keyboard Manager] editor: stop mappings silently turning OFF on list refresh`, and its commit message describes the same random-disable symptom and root cause in detail.
The issue has no assignee, no linked upstream PR, and no contradictory maintainer guidance that would justify a competing new design.

fix_assessment.rationale: Merged PR #49287 already fixes the exact Keyboard Manager editor state-flip mechanism described by this issue.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager's unified editor could silently flip a different mapping's persisted active state while rows were added, removed, filtered, or recycled. The reporter's "random enable/disable" symptom and the follow-up "enabled but not taking effect until toggled" symptom line up with an already-merged list-refresh fix.
known_information: The original report was filed against PowerToys 0.100.2 from a GitHub install, with the Keyboard Manager area selected.
The reporter says that when one line is added or removed, other lines are randomly enabled or disabled during editing.
A follow-up commenter reproduces the same problem on PowerToys v0.101.2362 stable on Windows 11 25H2 with Czech keyboard context, using a mix of key remaps, text remaps, and disabled remaps.
That follow-up also says some mappings appear enabled but do not actually take effect until they are toggled off and on again, and includes a recording attachment.
The issue is still open, has no assignee, and has no linked upstream PR in its live timeline.

The current Keyboard Manager editor row template binds each row's toggle to `IsActive`, and the current toggle handler contains a guard specifically intended to ignore recycle/binding-induced `Toggled` events.
inferences: The random enabled/disabled UI state and the "enabled but not active until retoggled" symptom are both consistent with the wrong mapping's persisted `IsActive` value being flipped during row recycling.
Because the merged fix is in the editor-only list-refresh path, this issue is more likely a pre-fix stable-build report than a new Keyboard Manager engine regression.
issue_context.analysis: Focused code and history review show that current upstream already has a precise fix for this symptom. The relevant code path is not a speculative match: the merged commit names the same failure mode, explains how recycled ListView containers re-fired the toggle handler, and adds a model-vs-control-state guard in the exact method that persists active-state changes. Existing-fix handling is therefore more accurate than opening a competing design.
initial_investigation: Read the complete upstream issue body, the later reproduction comment, labels, assignees, rename event, and absence of linked work in the timeline.
Inspected `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml`, where every editor row exposes `MappingEnabledToggle` bound to `IsActive`.

Inspected `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Pages/MainPage.xaml.cs`, especially `ToggleSwitch_Toggled`, whose current comment documents ListView container recycling causing unrelated mappings to turn OFF before the guard was added.
Reviewed merged PR #49287 and its fix commit `ba331c72d5eb6d164313dd9b2a4c5bf6373bf81f`, which explicitly targets "stop mappings silently turning OFF on list refresh".

Reviewed `src/modules/keyboardmanager/Tests/KeyboardManager.UITests/KeyboardManagerEditorTests.cs` to confirm the same editor surface already has persistence/toggle test coverage, even though the issue-specific list-refresh regression was fixed in the production handler rather than through a new linked issue.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed reproduction and the follow-up recording. This symptom matches the Keyboard Manager editor list-refresh bug fixed in merged PR #49287. That fix specifically guards the per-row enabled toggle so recycled list rows no longer flip a different mapping's persisted active state while mappings are added, removed, filtered, or scrolled. Because the follow-up reproduction is still on 0.101.2362 stable and the fix was merged afterward, the next step is to retest on a build that includes PR #49287 / the next release rather than opening a second fix design. If it still reproduces there, a fresh report should note whether it happens while filtering, adding, or deleting rows.
